description: A collaborative project changes primary ownership from one student to another, and the incoming person must reconstruct current status, assumptions, half-finished analyses, and open decisions from incomplete project materials.

user_profile.persona: 27-year-old PhD student inheriting a collaboration midstream
user_profile.context: The handoff was friendly but rushed, leaving too much tacit knowledge unstated
user_profile.communication_style: Patient and reconstruction-focused, wants to avoid repeating work

fact_sheet.fact: The official name of the research project is 'Project ChronoSynapse'.
The project's primary objective is to map functional connectivity changes in the default mode network of the aging human brain.
The Principal Investigator (PI) for Project ChronoSynapse is Dr. Aris Thorne, reachable at athorne@vdu.edu.
The previous student owner of the project was Leo Martinez, whose university email is lmartinez@vdu.edu.
The external collaborator is Dr. Elara Vance from the Helios Institute for Neuroscience; her contact is evance@helios.org.
For issues with the high-performance computing cluster, the contact is the Veridian Dynamics University HPC support team at hpc-support@vdu.edu.
The primary dataset for the project is a local collection named 'HCP-VDU-1200'.
Raw neuroimaging data in BIDS format is located on the Triton Cluster at the path: /data/triton/raw/chronosynapse/HCP-VDU-1200/.
The most recent set of preprocessed data generated by Leo Martinez is located at: /data/triton/processed/lmartinez/chrono_preproc_v2/.
All computational analysis is performed on the 'Triton Cluster', which is accessible via SSH at triton.vdu.edu.
The project's code is version-controlled in a Git repository hosted at git@git.vdu.edu:neuro-lab/chronosynapse.git.
The main development branch in the Git repository is named 'feature/dynamic_fc'.
The fMRI preprocessing pipeline is containerized using Docker; the definition file is `docker/Dockerfile.fsl` and the last known image tag is `chronosynapse-fsl:1.2`.
The last analysis run by Leo Martinez on the Triton Cluster was on 2023-10-15, job ID 784321, which failed after 12 hours due to a memory allocation error.
A key assumption in the `seed_correlation.py` script is that the posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) seed is a 6mm sphere centered at MNI coordinates (0, -53, 26).
The quality control script, `quality_control.sh`, has not yet been executed on subjects CSN_1100 through CSN_1150.
The lab's internal day-to-day communication occurs in the Slack workspace at vdu-neuro-lab.slack.com.
All project-specific discussions are consolidated within the `#chronosynapse` channel in the lab's Slack workspace.
The next scheduled progress meeting with collaborator Dr. Elara Vance is on 2023-11-08 at 10:00 AM PST via Zoom.
Notes from the last weekly sync with Dr. Thorne on 2023-10-23 are located in the Git repository at `/docs/meetings/20231023_notes.md`.
The project is funded by National Science Foundation (NSF) grant #21-54321.
The expiration date for the current NSF funding grant (#21-54321) is 2025-08-31.
The designated physical workstation for this project is 'NEURO-WS-04', located in Kepler Hall, Room 315.
The next major deadline is a conference abstract submission for the Society for Neuroscience (SFN), due on 2024-03-15.
A final decision has not been made on whether to use FDR or FWE for the statistical correction of group-level analysis results.
The purpose of an undocumented subdirectory, `exploratory_scrubbing`, within the preprocessed data folder is currently unknown.
The incoming student responsible for the project is Priya Sharma (psharma@vdu.edu).
The primary analysis scripts use Python 3.9 and require the `nilearn` library version 0.9.2.
Priya Sharma's personal home directory on the Triton Cluster is located at `/home/psharma`.
